title: Blue Jays erupt for 5 runs in the eighth to beat Red Sox 6-4, extend Boston’s skid to 5
author: The Associated Press
bullets: The Toronto Blue Jays defeated the Boston Red Sox 6-4 after a five-run eighth inning.
Kazuma Okamoto's RBI single and Myles Straw's two-run double were key moments for the Blue Jays.
Willson Contreras hit his 24th homer, but Boston matched its longest losing streak at five games.

title: Allston-Brighton residents divided over future of Jackson Mann Community Center, survey shows
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Survey shows split opinions on the Jackson Mann Community Center's future, with housing, school, or both options considered.
553 survey responses showed 190 favor housing, 171 favor a school, and 124 favor both in the redevelopment.
Mayor Michelle Wu will decide the center's future by year-end, with construction not starting until 2030.

title: Tour the Patriots’ new 160,000-square-foot training facility
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The New England Patriots unveiled their 160,000-square-foot New Balance Athletics Center at a ribbon-cutting ceremony.
The facility features a 15,000-square-foot weight room, a virtual reality room, and a spacious locker room with 92 lockers.
The center includes hydrotherapy amenities, dining areas, a player lounge, and spaces for future growth in football operations.

title: Man killed in stabbing inside South Station during rush hour, officials say
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A man was fatally stabbed inside Boston's South Station during rush hour on Wednesday evening.
Boston police responded to the stabbing at 5:33 p.m.; the victim died at a local hospital.
The suspect, described only as male, remains at large; police are reviewing video and witness accounts.

title: Body found at TD Garden, police say
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A body was found Wednesday evening near TD Garden, located at 100 Legends Way, Boston.
Police responded at 5:15 p.m. to reports of an unconscious person at the venue's parking garage.
Boston police are conducting an ongoing investigation into the individual's death.

title: Athol man charged with child pornography possession
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Kristopher Ambrozewicz, 35, from Athol, was charged with possession of child sexual abuse materials, announced the U.S. Attorney's Office in Massachusetts.
A search of Ambrozewicz's home revealed multiple videos on his cell phone containing child sexual abuse material, officials reported.
Ambrozewicz, involved with youth soccer and mental health services, will be arraigned in Worcester Federal Court on Thursday.

title: Police: Person held pregnant woman hostage with gun during dramatic chase on I-93 in Milton
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Dominic Hampton-Boyd, 31, allegedly held a pregnant woman hostage with a gun during a police chase on I-93 in Milton.
The suspect crashed into eight vehicles before attempting to flee on foot; he was arrested and a firearm was seized.
Hampton-Boyd is to be arraigned in Quincy District Court on multiple charges; the specific charges are not yet released.

title: Stoughton town manager contradicts police chief who accused him of tampering with Sandra Birchmore investigation
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Stoughton Town Manager Thomas Calter denies Police Chief Donna McNamara's allegations of tampering with the Sandra Birchmore investigation.
Calter refutes McNamara's lawsuit claims of harassment and discrimination, calling them 'baseless' and supporting an impartial investigation.
McNamara's legal team asserts evidence contradicts Calter's statements, as he faces a no-confidence vote from local unions.

title: Nearly 30 people arrested after investigation into drug trafficking in Western Mass.
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Twenty-eight people arrested in Chicopee, Holyoke, and Springfield in a drug trafficking investigation led by the FBI's Western Massachusetts Gang Task Force.
Authorities seized over 12 firearms, over one kilogram of cocaine, fentanyl pills, and heroin during the operation named 'Operation Pinky Promise'.
Hampden County DA's Office reports the group distributed cocaine, crack cocaine, and fentanyl; charges for those arrested are unspecified.

title: Patriots stock watch 2.0: Who’s rising and falling ahead of preseason opener?
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas show promising performances in recent Patriots practices.
Behren Morton is expected to get playing time as third-string quarterback in upcoming preseason game.
Weak performances from reserve cornerbacks without key players in joint practice against the Colts.
